facts.text: pumpy controls a Harvard syringe pump or a Mighty Mini piston pump over an RS-232 interface
The supported Harvard pumps are Pump 11, Pump 11 Plus and PHD2000
The supported features for the Harvard pumps are infuse, withdraw, set diameter, set flow rate, set target volume and wait until target volume
A pump is created on a Chain and the PHD2000 is created with an address
The example flow rate is in uL/min and the example target volume is in uL
PHD2000 requires withdraw, stop, infuse rather than withdraw, infuse
PHD2000 only takes notice of target volumes when it has been put into volume mode using the keypad
Chain opens a serial line with two stop bits, no parity and a 2 s timeout
A command is written as the pump address, the command text and a carriage return
Pump.__init__ stores the name, the serial chain, the two-digit address and the diameter, flow rate and target volume (initially None), then queries VER to check the pump and its address
setdiameter states that the Pump 11 syringe diameter range is 0.1-35 mm and the pump truncates precision beyond two decimal places
setdiameter sends MMD with the diameter and checks it with DIA
setflowrate takes microlitres per minute and says the range depends on the syringe diameter and is given by the Pump 11 manual
setflowrate sends ULM with the flow rate and checks it with RAT
infuse sends RUN and checks for the forward-running status character
withdraw sends REV and checks for the backward-running status character
Pump.stop sends STP and expects the stopped status character
Pump.settargetvolume takes microlitres, sends MLT and stores the target volume
PHD2000 overrides stop, sends STP and expects the '*' status character
PHD2000.settargetvolume takes microlitres, converts them to millilitres, sends MLT and stores the value back in microlitres
waituntiltarget polls VOL until the pump stops or two consecutive replies are equal
